name: Mexenone
summary: Old benzophenone sunscreen filter (benzophenone-10) known mostly as a contact and photoallergen in dermatology clinics.
lead: Mexenone (benzophenone-10, trade name Uvistat) is a benzophenone-derived sunscreening agent with the chemical name (2-hydroxy-4-methoxyphenyl)(4-methylphenyl)methanone (C15H14O3). It is chemically related to oxybenzone (benzophenone-3).

name: Gadusol
summary: Natural fish-roe UV absorber studied as a bio-derived sunscreen molecule; lab and computational work only, no human trials.
lead: Gadusol is a small natural UV-absorbing compound (C8H12O6), a substituted cyclohexenone, found in the eggs of fish and in some other vertebrates and invertebrates. It was isolated from cod roe, where it occurs at about 4 g per kg dry weight, and its structure was confirmed by synthesis in 1981. It is related to the mycosporine-like amino acids that organisms in high-sunlight environments use as natural sunscreens.

name: Umbelliferone
summary: Plant coumarin that absorbs UVB/short UVA and is listed as a sunscreen agent; actual evidence is lab chemistry and animal work.
lead: Umbelliferone (7-hydroxycoumarin, C9H6O3) is a natural coumarin found in plants of the carrot family (Apiaceae) such as carrot, coriander and garden angelica, and in hydrangea and asafoetida. It absorbs UV light strongly at about 300 to 325 nm and fluoresces blue, and is listed on Wikipedia as having been used as a sunscreen agent as well as an optical brightener and a fluorescent indicator.

name: Padimate A
summary: Obscure PABA-ester sunscreen filter, withdrawn in Europe in 1989 and never US-approved; essentially no modern research on it.
lead: Padimate A (isoamyl p-dimethylaminobenzoate, Escalol 506) is a PABA-ester UV filter, a dimethylated ester of 4-aminobenzoic acid. It is chemically related to padimate O (octyl dimethyl PABA), a much more widely studied sunscreen ingredient. Wikipedia states it was withdrawn in Europe in 1989 and was never approved for use in sunscreens in the US.

name: Benzophenone-9
summary: A water-soluble benzophenone UV filter with almost no published human data; mostly appears in environmental chemistry papers.
lead: Benzophenone-9 (BP-9) is a water-soluble benzophenone-type ultraviolet-absorbing compound that appears in lists of sunscreen and UV-filter ingredients. Published material on it is sparse and consists mostly of environmental and analytical chemistry rather than studies of cosmetic benefit.

name: HAA299
summary: An experimental UVA-1/visible-edge sunscreen filter with a small early study and an EU safety-committee opinion.
lead: HAA299, with the INCI name bis-(diethylaminohydroxybenzoyl benzoyl) piperazine, is an experimental organic UV filter designed to absorb long-wave UVA (UVA-1) and the violet edge of visible light. The EU's Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety (SCCS) issued a scientific opinion on a nano form of HAA299 in 2021, describing it as a UV filter intended for sunscreen products to protect skin against UVA-1 rays.

name: Acitretin
summary: A prescription oral retinoid for severe psoriasis and keratinisation disorders, with strict pregnancy-prevention rules.
lead: Acitretin is an oral second-generation retinoid used for severe psoriasis that has not responded to other treatments, and off-label for several disorders of keratinisation. It is the active metabolite of etretinate and is sold under brand names including Soriatane and Neotigason. It is a prescription-only drug in the US, UK, Canada and Australia.

name: Etretinate
summary: A withdrawn oral retinoid for severe psoriasis, replaced by acitretin because it lingered in the body for years.
lead: Etretinate (brand names Tegison, Tigason) is a second-generation oral retinoid developed by Hoffmann-La Roche for severe psoriasis and related keratinisation disorders. The US FDA approved it in 1986, and Roche voluntarily withdrew it from the Canadian market in 1996 and the US market in 1998 because of its very long elimination half-life and teratogenic potential. Wikipedia lists it as still marketed in Japan.

name: Alitretinoin
summary: A prescription retinoid for severe chronic hand eczema (oral) and Kaposi's sarcoma lesions (gel), not a cosmetic.
lead: Alitretinoin (9-cis-retinoic acid) is a naturally occurring retinoid that activates both retinoic acid receptors and retinoid X receptors. It is marketed as a topical gel (Panretin) for skin lesions of AIDS-related Kaposi's sarcoma and as oral capsules (Toctino) for severe chronic hand eczema unresponsive to potent topical corticosteroids. It was developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals.

name: Seletinoid G
summary: A Korean lab-designed retinoid for aging skin, tested only in a tiny short study and skin models.
lead: Seletinoid G is an experimental synthetic retinoid that was designed with computer-aided molecular modeling by Korean researchers as a topical anti-aging ingredient intended to cause less skin irritation than all-trans retinoic acid (tretinoin). Published work on it concerns aged and photoaged skin, with a related line of laboratory work on skin barrier repair.

name: Motretinide
summary: A largely historical topical acne retinoid with a 1984 trial against benzoyl peroxide and little modern literature.
lead: Motretinide is an aromatic retinoid, an analogue of retinoic acid, classed as a topical anti-acne agent (ATC code D10AD05). It has been described as a retinoid once used on the skin for acne; it is not among the retinoids in common use today.

name: Tazarotenic acid
summary: The active acid form of prescription tazarotene; evidence exists for the parent retinoid's photoaging effect, not for the metabolite alone.
lead: Tazarotenic acid is the active metabolite of tazarotene, a prescription topical retinoid. Tazarotene is a prodrug: after it is applied to the skin, esterase enzymes rapidly remove its ethyl ester group, producing the free acid that binds retinoic acid receptors . It is not sold as a separate product; people encounter it through tazarotene (brands such as Tazorac, Arazlo and Fabior) .
claims: Tazarotene is a stronger anti-aging retinoid than tretinoin
The metabolite is where the activity comes from

name: Oleyl adapalenate
summary: A newer adapalene-ester cosmetic retinoid with one small 2024 trial suggesting better wrinkle results and tolerability than retinol.
lead: Oleyl adapalenate (marketed as Adapinoid) is described in the literature as a third-generation retinoid and a pro-drug of adapalene, formed by joining adapalene to an oleyl group . It is used in cosmetic skincare creams aimed at photoaging, positioned as a retinoid with better tolerability.

name: Liarozole
summary: An older oral retinoic-acid blocker tested in psoriasis and ichthyosis, with no cosmetic evidence.
lead: Liarozole is an investigational imidazole-type drug classed as a retinoic acid metabolism blocking agent (RAMBA). It inhibits the cytochrome P450 enzyme that breaks down all-trans-retinoic acid, raising retinoic acid levels in tissues, and it also inhibits aromatase and CYP17A1 . It was studied orally for psoriasis, ichthyosis and prostate cancer .

name: Talarozole
summary: An investigational retinoic-acid blocker shelved for acne and psoriasis, now explored for osteoarthritis; no cosmetic evidence.
lead: Talarozole (formerly R115866; planned trade name Rambazole) is an investigational retinoic acid metabolism blocking agent (RAMBA). It inhibits the CYP26 enzymes, mainly CYP26A1 and CYP26B1, that break down all-trans-retinoic acid, so it raises retinoic acid signaling without supplying a retinoid . It was developed for acne, psoriasis and other keratinization disorders, and development for those skin uses is reported as discontinued .

name: Retinyl esters
summary: Vitamin A's storage esters, used in creams as gentler retinol alternatives; skin evidence is thin.
lead: Retinyl esters are fatty-acid esters of retinol (vitamin A), the main form in which the body stores vitamin A, chiefly as retinyl palmitate in the liver . In cosmetics, retinyl palmitate, acetate and propionate are used as milder, more stable alternatives to retinol and tretinoin .

name: Retinyl acetate
summary: A stable vitamin A ester used in foods and some skincare; no appearance trials exist.
lead: Retinyl acetate (vitamin A acetate) is a synthetic, fat-soluble ester of retinol. It is used to fortify foods such as margarine, plant-based milks and cereals, appears in multivitamins, and is included in some anti-aging skincare products, where it is presented as a more stable, gentler alternative to retinol .

name: Ceramide EOP
summary: A skin-barrier ceramide listed in moisturisers; little is published on this subtype specifically.
lead: Ceramide EOP is a skin ceramide, a waxy lipid made of a sphingoid base joined to a fatty acid, that appears on ingredient lists of barrier-repair moisturisers. Ceramides in general are a component of the stratum corneum lipid matrix, where, together with cholesterol and free fatty acids, they form the water-limiting barrier of the outer skin .

name: Hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid
summary: Chopped-up hyaluronic acid sold as the deeper-penetrating hydrator; direct evidence is thin.
lead: Hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid is hyaluronic acid (HA) that has been broken into shorter chains, and it is marketed in skincare as a low-molecular-weight form intended for deeper hydration. HA itself is a glycosaminoglycan found in skin and other connective tissues, where it supports hydration .

name: Sodium hyaluronate
summary: The salt form of hyaluronic acid in most moisturisers and serums; well established medically, with little direct data on topical looks effects.
lead: Sodium hyaluronate is the sodium salt of hyaluronic acid (HA), a linear polysaccharide of repeating glucuronic acid and N-acetylglucosamine units found in skin, joint fluid and the eye . It is the form usually listed in moisturisers and serums, and it is also used in medical products such as joint injections and ophthalmic surgical viscoelastics.

name: Tetrahexyldecyl ascorbate
summary: An oil-soluble vitamin C ester for serums; human data come from small, product-level studies.
lead: Tetrahexyldecyl ascorbate (THD ascorbate, THDA) is an oil-soluble ester derivative of vitamin C used in serums and moisturisers marketed for brightening and anti-ageing. It is used as an alternative to L-ascorbic acid, which is described as unstable and sometimes irritating at high concentrations .

name: Ethyl ascorbic acid
summary: A vitamin C ether sold for brightening; supported by lab studies, with no controlled human trials found.
lead: 3-O-ethyl ascorbic acid (ethyl ascorbic acid, EAC) is an ether derivative of vitamin C used in brightening and anti-ageing skincare. It is described as a tyrosinase inhibitor and is widely used in formulations, although the mechanisms behind its effects have been described as poorly understood .

name: Sodium ascorbyl phosphate
summary: A stable, water-soluble vitamin C derivative; formulation data are plentiful, human appearance outcomes are sparse.
lead: Sodium ascorbyl phosphate (SAP) is a water-soluble, phosphate-ester derivative of vitamin C used in cosmetics, mainly as an antioxidant. The Cosmetic Ingredient Review's safety assessment of ascorbic acid and its salts and esters, including SAP, describes them as functioning primarily as antioxidants in cosmetic formulations .

name: Magnesium ascorbyl phosphate
summary: A stable, water-soluble vitamin C derivative in brightening serums; common in products, thin on direct human trials.
lead: Magnesium ascorbyl phosphate (MAP) is a water-soluble derivative of vitamin C used as an ingredient in skincare products, where it is marketed as a more stable alternative to L-ascorbic acid. It is described in the literature as a pro-drug of vitamin C, meaning it is meant to be converted to ascorbic acid after reaching the skin.

name: Superoxide dismutase
summary: An antioxidant enzyme added to anti-aging products; biologically central, but cosmetic evidence is essentially unstudied.
lead: Superoxide dismutase (SOD) is a family of metalloenzymes that convert the superoxide radical into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide and is regarded as a first line of antioxidant defense in most oxygen-using organisms.  The enzymatic activity was identified in 1969 by James McCord and Irwin Fridovich in a copper protein from red blood cells.

name: Ubiquinone topical
summary: The mitochondrial antioxidant in many anti-aging creams; skin penetration is a recognized hurdle and direct wrinkle trials are scarce.
lead: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10, ubiquinone) is a fat-soluble, quinone compound found in cell membranes and involved in mitochondrial electron transport, and it also acts as an antioxidant.  It is included in some anti-aging creams, and the literature describes cosmetically applied CoQ10 as having been reported to reduce photoaging and wrinkle depth, while noting that its bioavailability through skin is poor.

name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1
summary: The collagen-signal peptide half of Matrixyl 3000; widely used, with mostly lab and permeation data behind it.
lead: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 (Pal-GHK) is a synthetic lipopeptide made of the amino acids glycine, histidine and lysine joined to palmitic acid, used in cosmetic skincare.  It is marketed as a collagen-stimulating signal peptide and is one of the two peptides in the branded blend Matrixyl 3000.

name: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7
summary: The anti-inflammatory peptide half of Matrixyl 3000; present in many serums, with little isolated human data.
lead: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 (Pal-GQPR, sold as Rigin) is a synthetic peptide of glycine, glutamine, proline and arginine attached to palmitic acid and used in anti-aging and sensitive-skin cosmetics.  It is described as an anti-inflammatory signal peptide and is the second peptide in Matrixyl 3000.

name: Matrixyl 3000
summary: Sederma's two-peptide anti-wrinkle blend; ubiquitous in serums, little independent human data on the blend itself.
lead: Matrixyl 3000 is a branded peptide complex made by Sederma that combines palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, and is used in anti-wrinkle serums.  Its predecessor, Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4), was launched by Sederma in 2000.

name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-5
summary: A collagen-signalling cosmetic peptide (Syn-Coll) with only multi-ingredient, small-scale evidence behind it.
lead: Palmitoyl tripeptide-5, sold under the trade name Syn-Coll, is a synthetic lipopeptide used as an ingredient in anti-wrinkle and skin-firming cosmetics. It is marketed as a "signal peptide" intended to prompt skin cells to make more collagen, and it appears in creams, serums and microneedle patches.
